problem: Existing VLN methods treat the instruction as one sequence, so key goal phrases are not emphasized. Prior external-knowledge methods (KERM, ACK, CKR) use text-only, generic commonsense knowledge that does not bridge the language-vision gap or fit the specific environment.
motivation: Alignment between linguistic goals and visual observations stays shallow and fragile in cluttered or occluded scenes. Providing concrete visual exemplars of goal phrases plus environment-specific textual descriptions could ground instructions better than abstract commonsense.
key_idea: Extract complete goal phrases with an LLM, use them to generate a diffusion-based image knowledge base, and build an environment-specific BLIP-2 caption knowledge base, then fuse both into DUET through gated attention augmentors.
insight: Neither knowledge source helps consistently alone: in the multimodal ablation on REVERIE val-unseen, image knowledge alone or text knowledge alone leaves SPL flat or slightly lower (32.68 and 33.18 vs 33.32), while both together give SPL 35.88 and RGSPL 24.86. Sigmoid gating matters, since disabling it on either pathway hurts SPL. An LLM phrase extractor (Qwen3-4B) beats SpaCy on SR/RGS (50.03 vs 47.94 SR), but its SPL and RGSPL are not better than SpaCy's in that ablation. Feature analysis suggests the augmentor compacts visual features and diversifies text features.
method: Subgoal Extraction: Qwen3-4B prompted to extract attribute-preserving noun phrases from the instruction (avg 4.3 per R2R instruction, 2.3 per REVERIE instruction).
Goal-Aware Augmentor: BERT instruction features act as queries and subgoal embeddings as keys/values in MHA; a sigmoid gate fuses the enhanced and original features.
Textual Knowledge Base: BLIP-2 with prompt 'a photo of' captions the 36 sub-views of each Matterport3D panorama (~380K entries); CLIP retrieves the top-5 entries per view.

Image Knowledge Base (R2R_GP / REVERIE_GP): Flux-Schnell generates images from '[subgoal] of the indoor environment in real estate' (~93K for R2R, ~50K for REVERIE); CLIP-B/16 features are pre-extracted and indexed per instruction.

Knowledge Augmentor: a correlation matrix between knowledge and target features is softmaxed to give a condensed knowledge representation, which goes into MHA and a sigmoid gate. It fuses image knowledge into the instruction and text knowledge into the visual features.
Action Prediction: DUET's dual-scale graph transformer (fine-scale and coarse-scale encoders) takes the enhanced visual and instruction features and predicts actions.

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer, LXMERT init, trained) with frozen Qwen3-4B, BLIP-2, Flux-Schnell and CLIP used offline for knowledge construction
setting.training_data: R2R and REVERIE training splits; pretraining with SAP, MLM, MRC (plus OG for REVERIE). The generated knowledge bases are the extra data (~380K captions, ~93K R2R images, ~50K REVERIE images).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP-B/16 features) plus topological map

numbers_note: R2R table values are printed as integers (SR/SPL/OSR) in the paper. The abstract's 'SR +5% / SPL +4%' for R2R test-unseen is not exactly consistent with the table (74 vs DUET 69 SR; 63 vs 59 SPL).
results: BTK reaches R2R test-unseen SR 74 / SPL 63 (DUET 69/59; GridMM 73/62; BEVBert 73/62). On REVERIE test-unseen it reaches SR 54.58, SPL 39.75, RGS 35.08 and RGSPL 25.23, with the best SPL, RGS and RGSPL among compared methods. Some baselines are higher on OSR/SR (VER, ViTeC).
limitations: Depends on pretrained generators (Qwen3-4B, Flux-Schnell, BLIP-2), whose quality can degrade for rare targets or fine-grained attributes, and generated images differ from real ones.
Costly offline construction (~120 h for text KB, ~60 h for R2R image KB and ~63 h for REVERIE) and higher inference overhead (+22M parameters, +11 ms/step, +6 GB VRAM).
The stopping decision remains a failure mode; evaluation is limited to discrete R2R and REVERIE in simulation.
